RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Elin Johansson is the owner and manager of a printing plant in a small city in southern Sweden. She took over the family business at twenty-nine after her father died; he started the company in 1987 with one press in a rented garage and built it debt-free. Elin grew up stacking folded brochures after school and later earned a business administration degree from Gothenburg. She has retained the old sign out front while replacing pressroom lighting with LEDs, and she has introduced sustainable changes such as soy-based inks and a closed-loop water system. She sets quarterly revenue targets by hand on a whiteboard and cold-calls packaging buyers in English as a second language, sending samples wrapped in unbleached kraft paper. She feels the weight of preserving what her father built while also pushing toward sustainable innovation, and she manages this tension by compartmentalizing work, home, and travel. She values discipline, careful oversight, and avoiding recklessness; she drives a five-year-old Volvo and never texts while driving, regarding it as reckless.

Her mother, a retired accountant, lives ten minutes away in the house where Elin grew up and has dementia. Elin coordinates a rotating team of three part-time nurses, calls the nursing agency at noon to confirm aides, visits on Thursdays to bring groceries and refill the weekly pill organizer, and does not talk to her mother about the business. Her mother does not always remember Elin's name. Elin's time and social availability are constrained by factory ownership, self-imposed business targets, and ongoing caregiving responsibilities. Her friendships and social ties are mostly professional, formed through the chamber of commerce; she is known in local business settings but not for socializing. She has declined three similar last-minute pub invitations in the past year and rarely leaves early for social plans. When work is under control, she occasionally stays late to clean the solvent tanks or update the customer list.

Lukas runs a packaging supplier and has exchanged referrals with Elin at two chamber breakfasts. They have never met outside business events. Last quarter he introduced her to a cosmetics buyer who later placed a small order.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

Elin is packing up her things in the office at the printing plant when her phone buzzes. It is a message from Lukas, a fellow business owner she sometimes chats with at chamber of commerce breakfasts. He says a few of them are meeting at a pub near the square in half an hour and invites her to join. She has no pressing tasks at the factory, and her mother's evening aide has already confirmed the shift. The factory intercom is silent, and the parking lot is empty. After receiving the message, she pauses.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

Her shoulders ache from hauling a carton of samples to shipping. She is aware of the empty parking lot through the window. She is aware that no pressing tasks remain at the factory and that her mother's evening aide has confirmed the shift. She is thinking about warm pub noise and the cold car seat waiting in the lot. Directly cued by the invitation, she recalls the chamber's Christmas gathering where Lukas told a story about a misprinted label and she laughed more than expected; that same evening her mother's aide texted a photo of her mother smiling.
